memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When portions were served to them from Joseph's table, Benjamin's portion was five times as much as anyone else's. So they feasted and drank freely with him." - Gen 43:34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The feast is generous, but Benjamin's portion is astonishing — "five times as much as anyone else's." Joseph lavishes special favour on his beloved younger brother, an extravagant, over-the-top gift far beyond what anyone could need. And the chapter ends on a note of joy: "they feasted and drank freely with him." What began in fear ends in celebration.

There is a quiet test hidden in Benjamin's fivefold portion. Years ago, these brothers had burned with jealousy when their father favoured Joseph with a special robe (Gen 37:3-4). Now the youngest is favoured again, lavishly, right in front of them. Would the old envy rise up? Remarkably, it did not. Instead, "they feasted and drank freely." The men who once could not bear a favoured brother now rejoiced with one. God had healed the jealousy in their hearts.

And notice the sheer extravagance of the favour — five times as much. This is a picture of grace, which is never merely adequate but overflowing. God does not deal with His children in stingy measures; He gives "immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine" (Eph 3:20). His grace is a fivefold portion, a cup that overflows (Ps 23:5).

Two things to carry away: rejoice when God blesses others, letting go of the envy that once might have consumed you; and receive God's extravagant grace toward you with wonder. He does not ration His goodness. Come to His table and feast freely.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can I rejoice when God lavishes favour on someone else?
2. Has God healed the jealousy that once gripped my heart?
3. Am I receiving God's extravagant, overflowing grace with wonder?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, heal any jealousy in my heart, and help me to rejoice when You bless others. Thank You that Your grace is never stingy but overflowing. Help me to feast freely at Your generous table. Amen.
